text: We can go around the world and survey more water-deprived countries.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: To put things in perspective, our public discourse needs to be supported by deep knowledge of subject matters in discussion.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Thankfully, our schools are doing a great job in injecting realism in learning.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Our teachers are taking learning beyond classrooms, into the community and overseas.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: We have more students at different levels participating in overseas exchange programmes than ever before.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: I would also argue that we should do more, for the population at large.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: For instance, the Government could invest more in media and content production, to help our public broadcast be even more comprehensive and interpretational in their news-reporting and analysis.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Complemented by our growing think-tank and research community, there is no reason why we cannot raise our average understanding of complex issues and the understanding of the world.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: I think the bottom line is, how do we watch the world "live" from Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: So, 70% in Singapore is one day on the Alibaba platform.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Budget 2017 builds upon a plethora of support programmes previously introduced.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: These programmes include SkillsFuture that help the workforce in general, and a whole host of productivity-related programmes that help SMEs.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: And they were all summarised just now by Minister Iswaran.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: There is really no shortage of support programmes.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: What we need is strong motivation from individuals, from firms and organisations.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: To develop strong motivation, there must be deep awareness of the world and the understanding of competition.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Singapore's challenge now is how not to be a victim of our own success.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: How can we leap from our comfort zone and overcome the false sense of security.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: It is not just physical connectivity that we need to build, but the psychological bridge to understand the world, to reach out to complex issues and to deal with them tenaciously.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: There is no silver bullet but hard work aplenty.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Trying to build for the future, for whom most discount the benefits of, and meeting short-term needs, for whom most place an emphasis on.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: But the future is not that far away and how we spend in the long term affects how we budget for the short term.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Uncle Koh came to see me a few weeks ago and he was in a fix.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Adventurous and enthusiastic in his 60s, he had tried being a Grab taxi driver.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: But he did not know how to use his phone to locate customers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: So, three days into the job, stressed out by the ordeal of fiddling with his phone till no end, Uncle Koh gave up and decided to be a cook instead.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: He took a course in culinary skills, used up his SkillsFuture credit and brought his shiny, laminated certificate to see me.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: He could not find a job, he said, as he did not have any prior experience being a cook.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: So, please, could he have more SkillsFuture credits so he can try something else?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This story encapsulates the challenges the future economy brings us as individuals, as businesses and as a government.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: For Uncle Koh, he could no longer cruise empty on the streets, burning up diesel, looking for customers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: He had to learn how to use a taxi-hailing app.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: He had SkillsFuture credits, but he had not used them where he needed it most.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: For firms, they can no longer rely on old business models as new entrants come in, disintermediating them and being asset-light, did not have the sunk costs that traditional firms bear.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: We have to make these investments work for us because every dollar spent on one item in the Budget, is another dollar not spent somewhere else.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Such an outcome-based approach where employers, trade associations and chambers, and unions are encouraged to develop training programmes for their workers because they know best the skills the marketplace values and thus the skills workers need to have, is the right move for SkillsFuture.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: With the integration of SkillsFuture Portal with Jobs Bank, the nexus between training and jobs will be even tighter.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Further, that individuals are guided by industry practitioners in their choice of training so that they are likely to choose relevant training which provides tangible benefits and, therefore, motivate them to train more.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: A more targeted approach in the delivery of training is more likely to deliver tangible outcomes.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: For the ITMs, their effectiveness is tied to the KPIs set out for them.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While it has often been said that we should not set static targets for the ITMs, given that they defer from industry to industry, and should be instead be "live" documents, having a vision on what the industry could look like and thinking through what the parameters for automation, innovation, labour and productivity can be, will give them something to work on, to try and possibly fail, to retry, and recalibrate.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: For how then will we − Government, firms and workers − know whether we are succeeding?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It requires great trust, collaboration and vision for firms, competitors, unions and Government representatives to come together and work effectively together.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I further suggest that disruptors, entrepreneurs from adjacent industries and also overseas markets be brought in, where possible, into the discussion on the ITMs to enrich the discussion and paint the possibilities or we might be entrenched in local models and local constraints.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: SkillsFuture and the ITMs are huge outlays to develop our capabilities.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How they are implemented affects their ultimate efficacy and we need to be clear as to the outcomes we hope to achieve, and have parameters to track their implementation and course-correct to ensure success.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: For only then will they be effective investments commensurate to the amounts we have allocated them in consecutive Budgets.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: That said, SkillsFuture and the ITMs form only part of the overall Budget.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: An analysis of how else we are allocating our resources will give a sense of how prepared we are for the future.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: However, since FY2015, we have been running a primary deficit where our total expenditure exceeds our operating revenue even before Special Transfers are considered.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: To ensure prudent expenditure, can we look to bind expenditures or match them with revenues, so that any increases in expenditure are carefully considered in relation to how the funds will be provided.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Given our reliance on NIRC to fund our Budget, what are the inherent risks we face?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Should there be huge changes in global outlooks of capital markets and earnings of firms, how does that change our expected long-term rates of return and our ability to use NIRC to fund our Budget?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: But these are taxes mostly to right-size behaviour and are not in the longer term derived from new economic activity.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The future economy has already been shown to bring new business models and new relationships between firms and workers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: With the growing importance of the sharing economy and cross-border transactions over Internet platforms, more thought should be put into how we can update our tax policies to keep in line with new emerging business models and maintain a level playing field.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Otherwise, the tax burden may fall unnecessarily on certain segments, or individuals and consumers over time.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Lastly, as more individuals participate in the New Economy through freelance work arrangements, we will need to ensure that our retirement adequacy frameworks take care of our citizens.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: One leg of the equation is missing if companies who engage individuals systematically to work for them do not pay CPF.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: And regulations may need to be tweaked to bring them into the fold.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Much has been said about how firms and workers need to be oriented to meet the challenges of the Future Economy.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The future may be uncertain but we need to make certain as much as we possibly can.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: We require daring, but we also require prudence.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: (In Mandarin):   Much has been said about how businesses and workers can meet the challenges of the future economy.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: What I would like stress is that the future may be uncertain but we need to make Singapore's success as certain as we possibly can.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Budget 2017 attempts to strike a balance between building for the future and meeting short-term needs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: SkillsFuture and ITMs are the two key pillars to help businesses and individuals to meet the challenges of the new economy.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Budget 2017 focused on "on the job skills utilisation" to ensure a better match between training and jobs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Outcome-based training is the right move for SkillsFuture.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I suggest that there be regular reviews of the training programmes under SkillsFuture to ensure they indeed generate desired job outcome.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: For ITMs, although industries differ from each other, having a vision of what the industry could look like and thinking through what the parameters for innovation, labour and productivity can be, will guide firms on their next move.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I hence suggest that entrepreneurs who are equipped with disruptive technologies and technology pioneers in the overseas market be brought into the discussion on ITMs to help our firms paint the future.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Given our reliance on NIRC, if the outlook of the international market changes, are we still able to fund our Budget?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Therefore, can we consider binding expenditures with revenues or performance?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Be it SkillsFuture, ITM or Government projects, can we determine how much we should invest in based on anticipated and quantifiable outcome?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Facing an uncertain future, we need to make Singapore's success as certain as we possibly can.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: We need to be daring, but also prudent.
